lastCompletedGameRecap.recapHeadline: Jets score on first 5 drives and edge Chargers 27-24 to snap 5-game skid
lastCompletedGameRecap.recapLeadExcerpt: INGLEWOOD, Calif.  -- — Mired in a losing season, New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith 's efficiency has been largely overlooked with the offense lagging.  Sterling Shepard helped change that Sunday, catching two touchdown passes from Smith and potentially earning himself a permanent promotion.  Smith completed 17 of 21 passes for 176 yards and another TD as the Jets scored on their first five drives to beat the Los Angeles Chargers 27-24 and end a five-game skid.
lastCompletedGameRecap.upNextNotes: Up next Jets: At Miami next Sunday. Chargers: Host New England next Sunday.

coachingMatchup.headline: Aaron Glenn & DC Brian Duker vs. HC Jeff Hafley, OC Bobby Slowik & DC Sean Duggan (Road Test)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting New York Jets's staff (Aaron Glenn, OC Frank Reich, DC Brian Duker) against Miami Dolphins (1-9)—testing both New York's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Aaron Glenn and OC Frank Reich pair condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to stress Miami Dolphins's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against Miami Dolphins's pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Brian Duker balances four-man pressure with disguised Quarters and Cover 6 split-safety rotations on early downs and in the red zone.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion discipline and red-zone touchdown rate govern whether New York sustains multi-play scoring drives or yields momentum to Miami Dolphins's pass rush and coverage disguises.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: Road Test situational play-calling, penalty margin, and turnover differential provide the clearest late-game swing factors for both coaching staffs.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Geno Smith, Mason Taylor & Garrett Wilson vs. CB Jason Marshall Jr. & LB Chop Robinson
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: NYJ: #21 Pass Off (207.7 yds) · #15 Off. Scoring (+0.90) | MIA: #28 Pass Def (+5.15)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Geno Smith, Mason Taylor & Garrett Wilson attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against Miami Dolphins's #28 pass defense (+5.15). Winning early-down timing throws keeps New York's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Geno Smith (#7) scanning Dolphins's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Chop Robinson widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for Mason Taylor (#85).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Harrison Phillips, Jowon Briggs & Darrell Jackson Jr. vs. QB Kyle McCord & OT Patrick Paul
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: NYJ: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | MIA: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Harrison Phillips, Jowon Briggs & Darrell Jackson Jr. lead New York's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against Miami Dolphins's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets Jets keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether Harrison Phillips (#97) draw chip help from Dolphins's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Jowon Briggs (#91).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Dane Belton, Azareye'h Thomas & Demario Davis vs. WR Malik Washington & QB Kyle McCord
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: NYJ: #26 Pass Def (+4.08) | MIA: #31 Pass Off (161.9 yds)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Dane Belton, Azareye'h Thomas & Demario Davis anchor New York's #26 pass defense (+4.08) against WR Malik Washington and Miami Dolphins's #31 passing attack (161.9 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces Dolphins into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track Dane Belton (#6) at the top of routes against WR Malik Washington: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB Kyle McCord's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Braelon Allen & Andrew Beck vs. Dolphins Front Seven & LB Chop Robinson
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: NYJ: #18 Rush Off (111.0 yds) | MIA: #2 Rush Def (-1.82)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Braelon Allen & Andrew Beck test Miami Dolphins's #2 run defense (-1.82) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes Dolphins's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether Dolphins's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for Braelon Allen (#0).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Armand Membou, Olu Fashanu & Josh Myers vs. DT Keith Cooper Jr. & Dolphins Simulated Pressures
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: NYJ: #16 Pass Protection (6.0%) | MIA: #16 Def Sacks (2.4/gm)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Armand Membou, Olu Fashanu & Josh Myers protect Geno Smith (#16 protection at 6.0%) against DT Keith Cooper Jr. and Miami Dolphins's #16 pass rush (2.4/gm). Passing off interior twists and simulated blitzes cleanly determines late-down conversion efficiency.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Armand Membou (#70) on obvious passing downs—if DT Keith Cooper Jr. cannot win clean around the arc, Dolphins must dial up interior stunts that stress Olu Fashanu (#74).
